title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 425
paragraphs: Having put these men to death, he next summoned the priests into his presence; and when the priests answered him in the same manner, he said that if a tame god had come to the Egyptians, it would not escape his knowledge. Saying this, he ordered the priests to bring Apis into his presence, and they went to bring him. Now this Apis, or Epaphos, is a calf born of a cow that is not permitted afterwards to conceive any other offspring; and the Egyptians say that a flash of light comes down from heaven upon this cow, and from it she produces Apis. This calf that is called Apis is black and has the following signs: a white square upon the forehead, on the back the likeness of an eagle, double hairs in the tail, and on the tongue a mark like a beetle.
